localBiteReport: The most recent available reports covering Choctawhatchee Bay and the Destin/Freeport area are from the week of September 18–24, 2026 (about 1–1.5 weeks old as of today). The fall transition is underway, and the inshore bite around Destin and Choctawhatchee Bay is described as one of the best of the year: redfish, flounder, and speckled trout are all responding to an abundance of bait that has become much easier to find in the mornings. Redfish are the standout target, with croakers and spot minnows as preferred live baits for bigger fish around bridge structure, while flounder are also mixing in well. Water temperature at this location today is 85°F. The September 4–10 report from Capt. Blake Nelson (Last Cast Charters, specifically covering Choctawhatchee Bay) noted that bait schools — primarily greenies — had pushed from deeper open water onto flats and into bayous, which was drawing Spanish mackerel but also setting up improving redfish and general flats activity expected to build through October.
